transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Nolan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Maya Rivera (Redwood CSM); Marta Ruiz (CISO), Evan Cho (Head of ML), Priya Shah (Counsel), Noah Liao (Infra), Sasha Reed (Product)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
Silverpine is evaluating Redwood for inference across both hosted and private deployments. Primary asks: firm no-train assurance, SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys, audit log retention and format, RBAC/SSO controls, and data residency for PHI-bearing prompts. Next steps include sharing SOC2/ISO docs, a DPA/no-train attestation, and scheduling a KMS technical deep dive.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO, KMS & HSM, data residency (EU/US), RBAC & SSO, audit logs & retention, prompt retention/no training on customer data, PII/PHI handling, private (VPC) deployment options.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Nolan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we realize this is a packed agenda, gonna run through the compliance items and then Samir will cover the KMS and private deployment flow. Marta, thanks for making time.
[00:14] Marta Ruiz: Sure, thanks. We're tight on time, trying to get a checklist of must-haves to present to legal and infra. Primary concern is: will our prompts or patient data ever be used to train any model? We need an explicit no-train commitment.
[00:28] Avery Nolan: Absolutely, that's a core ask we see from health customers. I'll cover our standard no-train language and our higher-assurance options. Samir, quick note on the deployment modes?
[00:36] Samir Patel: Yeah, quick preview — Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated capacity, and private VPC deployment. For Silverpine with PHI, most customers go private or dedicated with customer-managed keys. We support both on-prem-ish packages and VPC peering.
[00:50] Evan Cho: Clarify: if we use hosted with a no-train opt-out flag, does that get technical enforcement? Or is it contractual only?
[00:59] Jules Kim: There's two layers: contractual no-train in the DPA and technical settings that disable retention and any internal training pipelines. For hosted, you can opt out at account level; logs are ephemeral unless configured otherwise and we have an explicit flag for no-train that disables moving data into training buckets. 
[01:17] Marta Ruiz: We need cryptographic guarantees for keys — we prefer customer-managed KMS keys and HSM backed. Can you integrate with our Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS and tie it to the VPC deployment?
[01:29] Samir Patel: Yes. We integrate with customer KMS via standard KMS APIs, and we can support HSM-backed keys. For private deployments we can also mount an HSM or use bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flows. Note: rotation and audit logs are available and we can surface key usage in the audit trails.
[01:44] Noah Liao: On rotation, we need to ensure seamless rotations without dropping active sessions or breaking KV cache. Does Redwood provide automatic rewraps for model KV caches?
[01:55] Samir Patel: Good Q. We do key rewraps at the storage layer, and runtime holds an envelope key — rewraps don't invalidate KV caches. I will share the doc but short answer: yes, designed for live rotation. Might be slightly different across deployment modes but it's supported.
[02:12] Priya Shah: For the legal side, we need SOC2 Type II and an ISO 27001 statement plus the DPA. Also want the explicit 'no training on customer data' attestation we can put into our vendor security register. Is there any separate attestation for PHI-sensitive customers?
[02:28] Avery Nolan: We provide a standard no-train attestation and — for regulated customers — we can provide a heightened attestation that includes details on data handling and separation. We'll include SOC2 Type II, summary of our ISO posture, and a DPA template.
[02:42] Sasha Reed: On data residency: our product teams want all inference for EU patients to stay in EU region. Is the routing policy deterministic by tenant?
[02:53] Samir Patel: Yes, requests can be routed by policy — region pinning by tenant is supported. For hosted, you select the region; for private/VPC it's the customer's infra region. We also support fallback policies but those can be disabled for strict residency.
[03:08] Marta Ruiz: Audit logs — what fields do you capture? We need to see request metadata, redacted content, key ids, and who accessed what. Also retention window — our policies require 7 years for certain logs.
[03:21] Jules Kim: Audit logs include timestamp, request id, tenant id, model id, route id, key id reference, response and status codes, and actor (service principal or user). We can include redacted request hashes so you can verify content without storing PII. Retention is configurable; typical retention tiers are 90 days (default), 1 year, 7 years via archive. Longer retention often moves to a cold storage with export to S3/GCS within your control.
[03:46] Marta Ruiz: Important: hashes are fine but legal wants to be able to prove non-repudiation for access for investigations. Can you support immutable audit trails or append-only logs?
[03:57] Samir Patel: We support pushing logs to your SIEM or WORM (write-once) archive. Also HSM-backed signing of log batches is possible for deep forensics. We'll capture tamper-evident metadata.
[04:09] Evan Cho: On PII/PHI redaction: do you offer in-line tokenization or SDK hooks so we can pre-strip patient identifiers before sending?
[04:19] Jules Kim: We have SDK-level tooling and pre-processing libraries that teams use to mask or tokenise PII. There's also client-side preprocessing recommendations; some customers run a lightweight redaction proxy inside the VPC to ensure nothing leaves in the clear.
[04:33] Marta Ruiz: About training — can you explain technical controls again? We need concrete, reproducible proof that data isn't used to train models.
[04:42] Samir Patel: So there's three guarantees: 1) contractual: no-train clause in DPA; 2) configuration: account-level no-train flag that prevents data routing to any training pipelines; 3) operational: audit trail and storage policies showing retention and access. For customers wanting the highest assurance, private deployments + customer-managed keys + disabled telemetry are used, and we can provide logs demonstrating the data path was local-only.
[05:05] Priya Shah: And do you allow the customer to request deletion of any stored prompt traces, including intermediate caches?
[05:12] Jules Kim: Yes — we provide retention controls and an API for data deletion. Important nuance: for running inferences there are ephemeral caches (KV cache) that may exist in memory for the duration of session; persisted caches we can purge and we maintain deletion records.
[05:26] Sasha Reed: If we choose hosted but with strict no-train, how do you prove historically that nothing from our tenant leaked into model weights?
[05:36] Avery Nolan: We can provide a historical DLP-style attestations: storage access logs, training data inventories, and a signed attestation from our security team. Notably, our training pipelines are separate environments and have access controls; customers using the no-train flag are excluded from ingestion pipelines by design.
[05:55] Marta Ruiz: Can you summarize the differences between hosted+no-train and private in terms of legal defensibility?
[06:03] Avery Nolan: Hosted+no-train is good for low-friction use with contractual and technical protections; private provides the highest level of assurance — you control keys, network, and retention. Legal defensibility is stronger with private because Silverpine could assert direct custody of cryptographic keys and logs.
[06:18] Noah Liao: We want to validate key usage telemetry — can Redwood emit per-request key-id and wrap metadata so our monitoring sees which key was used per inference?
[06:28] Samir Patel: Yes, per-request metadata includes key-id and envelope id. We can emit that to your log collector or include it in the audit bundle.
[06:36] Evan Cho: A practical question about model variants: if you fallback to a smaller model as part of cost SLO, does that change the training policy? For example, if a fallback model is third-party and subject to other policies, is our data still on no-train?
[06:49] Jules Kim: Whenever we route request to a model, that model adheres to the tenant's no-train setting. If a model variant is not allowed under the customer's policy we can exclude it from the routing table. There are model-level labels and compatibility flags; we'll lock routes for Silverpine's account as needed.
[07:05] Priya Shah: Regarding certifications, can we get copies of the SOC2 Type II report and the ISO 27001 certificate? Also, any penetration test summary?
[07:15] Avery Nolan: We'll share SOC2 Type II report under NDA, ISO summary, and recent pentest abstracts. Full pentest reports are typically redacted but we provide executive summaries.
[07:26] Marta Ruiz: About RBAC and SSO — we need SCIM provisioning, SAML SSO, and role hierarchy compatible with our internal groups. Also want just-in-time (JIT) provisioning off or on?
[07:38] Samir Patel: We support SAML 2.0, OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and can honor your group mappings. JIT provisioning can be disabled if you prefer manual provisioning. For fine-grained RBAC, we support roles mapped to service actions and can offer attribute-based controls in private deployments.
[07:53] Sasha Reed: How do you scope access between product read-only personas and ops write personas?
[07:57] Jules Kim: Roles are policy-driven: least privilege by default. You can define read-only routes, limited keys per route, and restrict ability to export logs. We also support token-level permissions and session expiry policies.
[08:08] Marta Ruiz: On encryption at rest — do you encrypt everything with customer key by default in private deployments?
[08:15] Samir Patel: Yes, in private deployments we can enforce use of customer-managed keys for all persisted data. For hosted, you can opt into CMK for storage layers; some ephemeral caches are encrypted with service keys but can be wrapped with customer keys in dedicated capacity.
[08:29] Evan Cho: A tangent — you mentioned KV cache earlier, please be mindful in docs: sometimes transcripts say "KV cash" — just flagging that happened on earlier call.
[08:37] Samir Patel: (laughs) noted. We'll send the correct docs.
[08:42] Marta Ruiz: We also want to see an example of audit log record for a single inference: show the fields, how PII redaction looks, and how we can query.
[08:53] Jules Kim: We'll export a sanitized sample audit record and a schema. Also a query example for SIEM ingestion.
[09:01] Priya Shah: For contract language — we need the no-train clause to include definition of 'training', remedies, and audit rights. Can Redwood support vendor audits (on-site or remote) for the private deployment?
[09:14] Avery Nolan: For private deployments vendor audits are straightforward: we can provide remote evidence or, subject to SOW, support on-site reviews. For hosted we offer remote audit packs and log exports.
[09:27] Marta Ruiz: Regarding incident response, do you have SOC incident procedure and SLA to notify customers within X hours? We require initial notice within 24 hours for breaches affecting PHI.
[09:39] Jules Kim: Our incident playbooks include a 24-hour notification SLA for incidents meeting threshold; we also have escalations and a dedicated security point-of-contact for enterprise customers. We'll include an incident response summary.
[09:53] Noah Liao: A practical ask: can you provide a checklist of the items we need to complete to onboard private VPC deployment? Firewall rules, peering steps, KMS config, DNS stuff.
[10:03] Samir Patel: Yes — we'll share the onboarding checklist and a step-by-step runbook.
[10:08] Evan Cho: About data deletion proofs: can you show a deletion certificate or signed record that a particular prompt ID was deleted?
[10:18] Samir Patel: We can provide deletion receipts — signed metadata showing item id, timestamp, operator, and hash of deleted data. For extra assurance we can include HSM-signed tokens.
[10:27] Priya Shah: On cross-border transfers: if a clinician in EU contacts a specialist in US via our product, will Redwood route traffic outside the EU?
[10:36] Samir Patel: Only if your routing policy permits cross-region fallback. For strict residency we recommend disabling fallback and pinning tenant routing to EU. If you need cross-border flows we can surface consent and legal basis controls.
[10:47] Marta Ruiz: Ok, we're close to time — can we recap next steps?
[10:52] Avery Nolan: Sure — recap: 1) We'll send SOC2/ISO and pentest summary (Avery) by Friday, 2) Samir to share KMS integration docs and VPC runbook by Monday, 3) Legal to receive no-train attestation and DPA draft (Avery/Maya) by next Tuesday, 4) schedule KMS technical deep dive with Noah and infra the week after.
[11:13] Priya Shah: Also please include sample audit log record and deletion certificate example.
[11:18] Maya Rivera: We'll include pilot pricing options and a suggested cadence for a POC.
[11:22] Marta Ruiz: Great. Thanks everyone.
[11:24] Avery Nolan: Thanks all. We'll get the artifacts over and follow up in email.

End of transcript.
